Hi all — thanks for the details, Adi. Short answer: Redwood's standard is PO-required for all goods and services to ensure proper coding and budget controls. That said, Procurement can approve limited exceptions on a case-by-case basis with the right controls.

What we need to evaluate/approve a temporary no-PO exception:
- Completed onboarding paperwork (we have vendor_onboarding_form.pdf and W-9) — thank you.
- Signed vendor terms or MSA (or confirmation that an MSA is in process)
- A succinct business justification from the owning AE (Adi) describing why the exception is needed, the dollar cap, and an expiration date for the exception (e.g., single invoice or 30 days).
- Proof of insurance / COI if services include on-site work (not necessary here but please flag).

I attached a short template we use for no-PO exception requests (no_po_exception_template.docx). Send the completed justification back here and I will run the approval. If approved, Finance will create a temporary vendor record and a routing instruction so the invoice can be paid without a PO for the capped amount.

Two operational notes: any no-PO approvals are time-limited and have a spend cap (typically <= $5k for pilot exceptions). Exceptions must be documented in the procurement system for audit.

Laura Bennett
Head of Procurement
Redwood Inference
